![](../../assets/images/pmxNODE-sticker.webp){fig-alt="pmxNODE hex sticker" fig-align="right" width="140"}

Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (NODEs) are a machine learning approach that combines the concepts of ODEs and Neural Networks (NNs). In short, NODEs are ODEs with one or multiple NNs on the right-hand side of the differential equation. They allow complex, dynamic data to be fitted without knowing the exact structural form of the ODE.

In the process of integrating NODEs into pharmacometrics, we developed [low-dimensional NODEs](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-023-09886-4). The aim was to integrate pharmacometric principles into NODEs and reduce the size of the required NNs. This further allowed us to implement [low-dimensional NODEs in pharmacometric software](https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13265), such as Monolix, NONMEM, and nlmixr2. Additionally, inter-individual variability could be applied to the parameters of the low-dimensional NODEs, making them a promising tool for pharmacometrics.

To make low-dimensional NODEs in Monolix, NONMEM, and nlmixr2 more accessible, I created the R package [pmxNODE](https://cran.r-project.org/package=pmxNODE), available on CRAN. It allows you to use NN functions within your structural model, which are then translated into the required equations.
